exclusions.A: His fence would go up in two days, it would hold her ram, and it would stand well back from the stream.
exclusions.C: Dell Haskett drove up from the fencing yard in Orley with wire in his truck and a cost lower than her feed bill, and I was on his side before he finished.
exclusions.D: So I joined her every Saturday, grudgingly, with Haskett's pitch about two-day fences still running through my head.
exclusions.E: His fence would go up in two days, it would hold her ram, and it would stand well back from the stream.

WV11-P01.4.note: Haskett's "pitch about two-day fences" is the sales case he made (cheap, fast, holds the ram) that won the narrator over before he finished.

exclusions.B: "When I was your age there were forty ewes on that slope, and now there are eleven and one ram," she said.
exclusions.C: "When I was your age there were forty ewes on that slope, and now there are eleven and one ram," she said.

exclusions.E: She stood there with her hand on the stone until the light was gone.

WV11-P01.5.note: Looking at the empty lower field, recalling forty ewes now down to eleven, and lingering until dark shows quiet longing for the past, not worry, thanks, amusement or annoyance.
